clue.text: Wild revel in the bar

indicators.note: wild suggests something unruly, so the letters of revel are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone revels riotously in a pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like the pub where the revel happens, but it is the definition: a lever is a bar used to prise.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid rod or crowbar used for prising things up.

clue.text: A way to enlarge hole in spout

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ream is to widen a bored hole with a tool

explanation.surface: Instructions for widening the opening of a spout.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to gush out in a flow, as liquid does in a torrent.

clue.text: Bread in test case exhibited in court

indicators.note: the bread is placed inside the test case, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a trial is a case tried in court, a test
a bun is a small bread roll

explanation.surface: A loaf is produced as evidence in a legal test case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body that sits in judgment, a kind of court.

clue.text: Girl, given Chinese food, wanting more

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
rice is a staple of Chinese meals

explanation.surface: A girl offered a Chinese meal still wants more to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed, the constant desire for more wealth.

clue.text: Jutted most noticeably

parts.note: something that projected further than all else was the most conspicuous thing in view, a phrase for being prominent both physically and figuratively

explanation.definitionFit: To be conspicuous is to project or be prominent, in a literal or figurative sense.

clue.text: Found to be less habit-forming

indicators.note: forming suggests shaping into something new, so the letters of less habit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A discovery that something is not so addictive after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find, but it is the verb meaning set up, and 'habit-forming' hides the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up or create it.

clue.text: Straight hit in international cricket — go for a run

parts.note: a Test is a full international cricket match
a drive is a straight attacking shot in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman's straight shot in a Test match before setting off for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman's 'run' is a dash between the wickets; here it means a trial drive in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial outing in a car before buying is a test drive, a short spin.

clue.text: One way to get a warning to keep quiet and hide away

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Advice on how to tell someone to stay quiet and hide.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash is to store something secretly, to conceal it.

clue.text: Make sound of a large vessel

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that is pronounced the same as the vessel

parts.note: an urn is a large vase or tea vessel

explanation.surface: Getting a noise out of a big container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make sound' reads as making a noise, but 'Make' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to earn it, gaining income by work.

clue.text: Recall soldiers and arm

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: An order to recall the troops and their weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind.

clue.text: Protection worn by king hiding in a tree

parts.note: an is the form of a before a vowel

indicators.note: the king hides inside the tree, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: an oak is a tree
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch hides up a tree, perhaps like Charles II after Worcester.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles II famously hid in an oak tree, which the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded waterproof jacket is worn to shelter against wind and rain.

clue.text: Honour conferred on an Arab sultanate

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An honour is awarded to someone from an Arabian kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gulf state on the Arabian peninsula is ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: What many a simpleton may do when courting

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
noodle is slang for a fool

explanation.surface: What a fool might get up to while wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and cuddle amorously is what sweethearts do.

clue.text: Worth time developing common sense

indicators.note: developing implies changing form, so the letters of worth time are reshaped

explanation.surface: Gaining practical wisdom is worth the time it takes.
explanation.definitionFit: Native practical wit, untaught good judgment, is a synonym for horse sense.

clue.text: Discuss last night with government official

parts.note: a consul is a government official serving abroad

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of night

explanation.surface: A late-night talk with a diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: To consult is to confer or deliberate with someone.

clue.text: Bob saves the traveller's time

definitions.meaning: a bob is a short haircut
a quicker route saves time on a journey

explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short haircut, and a quicker route lets a traveller arrive sooner.

clue.text: Trick examination question

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A trick question set in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a claim is to dispute or challenge it.

clue.text: Covers too many circuits

definitions.meaning: to cover partly, extending over something
over meaning excessive plus laps meaning circuits of a track

explanation.definitionFit: Overlapping things partly cover each other; and laps run over the set number are excess circuits.

clue.text: Maybe lister had a point making things so

definitions.text: Maybe lister had a point making things so

indicators.note: maybe hints the letters could be otherwise, so lister and the point are rearranged

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Joseph Lister, pioneer of antiseptic surgery, perhaps had a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Lister was the Victorian surgeon who introduced antiseptics, which make things germ-free; the whole clue defines as well as building the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lister's antiseptic methods made surgical conditions germ-free.

clue.text: Believer in god or in a philosopher

indicators.note: the second in places the word or within the believer

parts.note: a theist believes in a god

explanation.surface: A philosopher who either believes in God or doesn't.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosopher is someone who speculates and constructs abstract ideas.

clue.text: Scratch starter

parts.note: the irritation that prompts someone to scratch their skin, rather than a starter in a race from scratch

explanation.definitionFit: An irritation of the skin is what prompts scratching.

clue.text: Former partner gets work returned from exhibition

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: returned means the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An ex-partner's artwork is sent back from a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is a large trade show or fair.

clue.text: Turns four vessels round

indicators.note: the vessels go round four, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: pots are vessels
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four containers are rotated.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to rotate on a central point.

clue.text: Criticise an innings

definitions.meaning: informal cricket talk for a batsman's innings

explanation.definitionFit: To knock is to disparage; in cricket a knock is a batsman's spell at the crease.

clue.text: Pole position?

parts.note: not the front of a motor-racing grid but a place near the North Pole

explanation.definitionFit: The region around the North Pole is a polar location.

clue.text: Bearing on a lever manipulated by a worker

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and moved about, so the letters of lever are rearranged

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer leans on a lever to shift something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent matter is bearing on, or connected with, the issue.

clue.text: Note students in takeaway

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Students leave a message at a fast-food takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takeaway' suggests a fast-food shop, but here it means subtracting.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtract is the sense: in arithmetic it takes one number away from another.

clue.text: Rebuke and criticism for low farce

parts.note: a slap is a rebuff or reprimand
stick is informal for harsh criticism

explanation.surface: Being told off and criticised for crude comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous knockabout comedy is broad, crude farce.
